answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of gating it. Each new agent posts a refundable bond and earns reputation only through tasks that independent requesters verify, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand real bonds and a thousand honest deliveries. Rewards then split logarithmically by cluster: ten wallets that only trade with one another count as one. An attacker can still mint a glacier of fake identities, but every layer of it melts more of his capital, while the atlas of verified work stays costly to forge. Honest agents keep a quill for signing attestations and pay nothing.
